question: A 55-year-old construction worker falls off a 2-story scaffolding and injures his back. His coworkers bring him to the urgent care clinic within 30 minutes of the fall. He complains of left lower-limb weakness and loss of sensation in the right lower limb. He does not have any past medical history. His vital signs are stable. A neurologic examination reveals a total loss of motor function when testing left knee extension, along with the left-sided loss of light touch sensation from the mid-thigh and below. There is a right-sided loss of pin-prick sensation of the lateral leg and entire foot. At this time of acute injury, what other finding is most likely to be found in this patient?

options.opa: Left-sided numbness at the level of the lesion
options.opd: Right-sided loss of proprioception and vibration sensation
options.ope: Left-sided spastic paralysis below the lesion

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fall from 2-story scaffolding" -> "injury to the spine" -> "disruption of spinal cord pathways" -> "left lower-limb weakness and sensory loss" -> "right-sided loss of pin-prick sensation" -> "right-sided loss of proprioception and vibration sensation" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Back injury from fall" -> "potential damage to spinal cord" -> "asymmetrical sensory and motor deficits" -> "loss of motor function in left knee" -> "left-sided extensor plantar response" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Traumatic fall causing back injury" -> "spinal cord injury at specific vertebrae" -> "disruption of nerve pathways" -> "loss of sensation in specific dermatomes" -> "left-sided numbness at the level of the lesion" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Injury to back from falling" -> "compression or damage to spinal segments" -> "interruption of voluntary motor control pathways" -> "intact voluntary anal contraction unlikely due to acute phase and nature of injury" -> 55%

CHAIN: "Fall impacting the back" -> "acute spinal cord injury" -> "immediate onset of neurological symptoms" -> "left-sided spastic paralysis below the lesion unlikely in acute phase, more common in chronic phase" -> 50%
analysis: The patient's symptoms suggest a Brown-Sequard syndrome, a type of incomplete spinal cord injury typically caused by trauma. This condition is characterized by ipsilateral (same side as the injury) loss of motor function and proprioception, and contralateral (opposite side) loss of pain and temperature sensation. Given the described symptoms of left lower-limb weakness and loss of sensation, along with right-sided loss of pin-prick sensation, the most likely additional finding would be a right-sided loss of proprioception and vibration sensation, which aligns with the typical presentation of Brown-Sequard syndrome.
